title: CRLR/672/2019 of NAVJOT SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
CRLR No.672 of 2019
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.

Mr. Mehboob Rahi, Advocate holding brief of Mr.
Abhishek Verma, Advocate for the revisionist.
 Mr. P.S. Bohra, AGA for the State of Uttarakhand.
 The present criminal revision is arising out of an
order dated 11.11.2019 as passed by the Judge Family
Court, Haldwani in Criminal Misc. Case No.64 of 2019,
Gurjeet Kaur vs. Navjot Singh. By virtue of the
impugned order under challenge, the learned Family
Court has granted an interim maintenance to the tune of
Rs.3,500/- to be paid to applicant no.1 i.e. the wife and
Rs.15,00/-per month to be paid to minor daughter.
Apart from it, he has also been directed to pay a sum of
Rs.2,000/- as a consolidated amount to meet the
expenses of the proceedings.
 In the pleadings raised before the court below, in
defence, the revisionist has come up with the case that
he is working as worker in a jewellery shop, having an
income of Rs.6,000/- per month. In support thereto, he
has filed his income tax returns for the financial year
2019-20 in order to substantiate that he is having an
income of Rs.6,000/-. Whereas on the contrary the
evidence, which has been adduced by him in the
proceedings before the Mahila Help Line on
20.06.2019, he has contended that his wife not working
in the home and was never required to discharge any
domestic responsibility for the reason being that he was
having sufficient number of workers working in his
residence and in these circumstances, this Court is of
the view that a person could only afford the services of
servants in home when he has got handsome income to
meet the salary of the workman and that too also in
which he would be able to pay them. In view of such a
statement where he admits the fact that he has got
servants serving in his home, this fact itself will amount
to an inference to the effect that he has got sufficient
income to meet day to day liability, which the
respondent-wife and his daughter is supposed to have
for their sustenance .
 In that view of the matter, the reasoning which has
been assigned by the Family Court while deciding the

application, paper no.5 kha under Sub Section (2) of
Section 125 of Cr.P.C. this Court is of the view that the
judgment and order impugned dated 11.11.2019 does
not suffer from any apparent error on the face of the
record and consequently, this Court declines to exercise
its revisonal jurisdiction as against the impugned order.
Consequently, the revision lacks merit and accordingly,
the same is dismissed.
 After the dictation of the judgment concluded, the
learned counsel for the revisionist has submitted that an
appropriate direction be issued to the Family Court to
decide the main application under Section 125 of
Cr.P.C. itself within a stipulated time frame.
Considering the aforesaid request the Family Court,
Haldwani is requested to decide the Criminal Misc.
Application No.64 of 2019, which has been preferred
by the respondent under Section 125 of Cr.P.C, itself is
requested to be adjudicated within three months from
the date of production of certified copy of this order.
